cards.body:
## Summary
The phone and the TV can be in two different Linga activities at once, and the phone obeys the wrong one. A level check that was left (stop, Not now, Esc, or just choosing a situation from the menu) is kept forever, and while it is kept the phone shows the check instead of the rehearsal the TV is running. The learner speaks to Jamie and the phone sends it to the level check; on the topic question that reply becomes their stored goal. The conversation got a turn table in the last challenge; the level check, which has the same shape of loose fields, did not, and nothing decides which of the two owns the desk.

## Description
Two session slots, s.conversation and s.check, both persist and both can be live. Seven places pick the owner by hand and every one of them picks the check first (view.ts:170-178, 186-189, 196-208, 531-535; LingaTV.tsx:26, 47-55; LingaPhone.tsx:22, 62-64). Only three commands ever clear a check (level-self, plan-agree, a learner change), so a check abandoned at any stage outlives every scene started after it. Starting a scene never looks at the check (conversation.ts:128-148) and resuming one never does (conversation.ts:160). The result, shown by a probe against the real modules: with the TV on a rehearsal, the phone's answer is plan-goal (the reply is saved as preferences.goal and lost to the conversation) or check-answer (the reply is judged as a level-check answer).

The move is one small module, activity.ts, with two parts, both pure and imported by the server, the view, the TV and the phone exactly as turn.ts is. First, ownerOf(session): which of check, conversation or neither holds the phone now, decided once. A check is parked (a new optional LevelCheck.parked) when a scene starts or resumes, and a live conversation is paused when a check opens, resumes or restarts, so at most one is live; a parked check is not lost: home offers it as 'Carry on' (the existing check-part-way state) once the scene is finished or left. The 2026-09-25 owner decision is kept: with the TV on Linga home and a check left part-way, the phone still holds the check. Second, a check table in the shape of turn.ts: CHECK_STATES (about asked, reading, tasks between, say, listen, choose, verdict, plan asking the goal, plan topics, plan empty), ACCEPTS per state, checkAccepts and a refusal sentence. checkCommand asks the table once instead of its 8 stage guards, so plan-renew while the goal is asked, plan-add while the goal is asked and check-retry on the verdict are refused (409) instead of silently doing nothing or adding a topic no screen shows, and the view disables, from the same table, whatever the server would refuse.

## Flow
- Learner leaves the topic question, picks Booking from the menu: the check is parked, the phone shows Reply to Robin, the reply lands in the conversation.
- Learner finishes the rehearsal: home reads 'Find your level, you stopped part way: Carry on', and Carry on unparks the check where it was.
- Learner presses Find my level mid-scene: the scene pauses, the phone shows the check; Resume parks the check and the phone returns to the scene.
- Any client sending a check command the state does not take gets 409 and a sentence, and the view never drew that button enabled.

## Expected impact
Closes a path on which a reply is silently misfiled (a rehearsal reply stored as a goal, or scored as a level answer) and which the UAT run shows half the Characters can reach. Replaces 8 ad hoc guards and 3 unguarded commands with one table the server, the view and both devices share, so the next check feature (a second task kind, a plan-review step) is one row, as the next turn feature now is. The phone and the TV can no longer disagree about which activity is live.

## Evaluation
Claim: one ownerOf and one check table make the phone and TV agree on the live activity and make the server refuse exactly what the table refuses.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (cases 1-6 red; 7 and 8 are guards, green by design, so 0 of 6 behaviour cases)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first in tools/linga-rules-test.cjs, then npm test in desk/
Result: better
Gate: architecture

cards.body:
## Summary
A Linga learner works toward a certificate the desk never shows them. They finish a whole plan, home says 'Every topic talked through', and no certificate arrives, because two of the six skills a B1 certificate asks for were never in any topic. Nothing on any screen says what is missing, and 'Talk again' starts the first topic over. A learner who picked their level by hand can never be issued one at all and is never told. The desk already holds everything needed: what the band requires, what has been shown, what has not.

## Description
The certificate (W10) is issued by code when every required skill is 'on your own' and the latest record is a level check with medium or high confidence. The requirement is the band's base skills (cert.ts:35-52) widened by the skills of the agreed plan's topics (cert.ts:76-80). Three things leave the learner blind. One: a plan is only asked to span four skills (check.ts:159) while B1 needs six, and a scene records evidence only for its own focus skill, its review skill and repair (conversation.ts:218), so a certificate is reachable only if the plan or the learner's own situation choice happens to cover the rest. Two: recommendScene (curriculum.ts:83-110) never reads the requirement, so the 'next topic' and 'Talk again' ignore it. Three: the certificate surface does not exist until one is issued (view.ts:350-352 and 433), and a hand-picked band, which never certifies (cert.ts:68), says nothing.

The move has one pure function and three places that read it. certGap(learning) in cert.ts returns the band, which required skills are shown (with spoken or written, from the same evidence the plate uses), which are open, and the blocker when none can be issued (a hand-picked band, a low-confidence check, no check). Then: (1) recommendScene prefers, once the unstarted plan topics are done, a plan topic or built-in situation that practises an open skill, so 'Talk again' and the phone's Next topic lead somewhere; unstarted plan topics still lead first. (2) The TV's certificate screen, which today is a 'No certificate yet' page, becomes the plate in outline: the band and its name, the skills already shown as on the issued plate, and the open ones as dashed empty slots, in the Open Door's own dashed-path grammar (the Stones), with no number anywhere. A hand-picked band shows the plate without slots and one caption sentence, with Find my level as its action. (3) The menu door 'My certificate' appears for any learner with a record of checks, not only after one is issued. The picture is the verdict; the caption is one sentence of under 25 words. The TV never asks for typing and puts no answer on screen: it names skills, never a quote or a phrase to say.

## Flow
- Learner finishes the last plan topic. Home: 'Every topic talked through'; Talk again now starts Understand and repair, the first open skill, not the first topic.
- Menu, My certificate: the B1 plate in outline, four skills filled (spoken, written), two dashed slots; caption 'Each empty slot is a conversation still to have.'
- Learner whose level was picked by hand opens it: the plate with no slots, 'A certificate rests on a level check you take with Linga', and Find my level.
- The certificate issues as today when the last slot fills; the outline becomes the plate with its quote.

## Expected impact
Turns the reward from a surprise that may never come into a path the learner can see and walk, with no score and no count. Makes the end of a plan lead to the skills a certificate lacks instead of repeating the first topic, and tells a hand-picked learner the truth once instead of never. The data (placements, plan, evidence, achievements) is already on the record; no stored shape changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: certGap derives what a certificate still needs; recommendScene, the certificate screen and the menu act on it, and the plate stays free of digits, counts and game words.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (cases 1-3 and 5-7 red; case 4 is a guard and case 8 is the operator capture)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first in tools/cert-rules-test.cjs, then npm test in desk/, then the Playwright capture
Result: better
Gate: direction
